cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here would be about sweep TIMING rather than about the defect. It must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: a container was freed before the hash table it owns was torn down
object: the wspstat_t tap state, one g_new
lifetime_ender: g_free(sp), the container, while the teardown of what it owns is still to come
shape: a free ordered before the teardown of what the object owns
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `g_hash_table_foreach(sp->hash, ...)`, which loads `hash` from the freed struct.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: the error path was replaced wholesale -- v4.6.8:ui/cli/tap-wspstat.c calls `wspstat_finish((void *)sp);` (3 occurrences of `wspstat_finish` in the file), so the defective ordering no longer exists. A fix-reversal against history.
nested_why: the object came straight from g_malloc / g_new / g_new0 / g_strdup / getline -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no wmem allocator between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../wmem-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the stale read is a FIELD LOAD rather than a use of the pointer itself: the next two lines both need `sp->hash`, and the struct holding it is already gone -- so the fix is a REORDERING, moving the free below the teardown, and no null assignment would have helped.
